summary: A 1970 note by Steve Crocker about a Network Working Group meeting.
questions: how often did the early network group meet
subtitle: Announcement of the next Network Working Group meeting

tldr.problem: The Network Working Group needed to schedule regular meetings to coordinate protocol development and address emerging issues across the growing ARPANET.
tldr.mechanism: Following the November 1970 Houston meeting, Steve Crocker announced that general NWG meetings would be held approximately every three months, with Spring and Fall meetings synchronized to the Joint Computer Conferences.
tldr.outcome: The next meeting was scheduled for February 17-19, 1971 at the University of Illinois, establishing a regular cadence for in-person protocol discussions.

today: RFC 85 is a short announcement that established the pattern of regular face-to-face meetings for ARPANET protocol coordination. This practice continues in modern Internet standards work through IETF meetings, which occur three times per year. The formal meeting schedule helped transition the ARPANET from ad-hoc coordination to structured protocol development.

sections.title: Meeting Schedule Established
sections.content: In late December 1970, Steve Crocker announced the schedule for Network Working Group meetings based on the consensus from the Houston conference in November. Meetings would occur approximately every three months, with the major Spring and Fall meetings synchronized to the Joint Computer Conferences, spreading other meetings around to different sites to promote exposure and distribute the burden of hosting.
sections.plainLanguage: The group decided to meet regularly - a big meeting in spring and fall at conferences, and smaller meetings in between at different places.

sections.title: The February 1971 Meeting
sections.content: The next meeting was scheduled for February 17-19, 1971 at the Illini Union at the University of Illinois. Prospective attendees could contact Phyllis Ewing at the Center for Advanced Computation, arriving on the 17th. This meeting promised to be more organized than previous ones and would include prepared reports from participants, representing a shift from informal discussions to more structured presentations.
sections.plainLanguage: People would meet in Illinois in mid-February, and it would be more organized with actual prepared talks instead of just arguing.

sections.title: Coordinating the Network Community
sections.content: Regular meetings established a formal governance structure for the Network Working Group, moving it beyond ad-hoc discussions. By scheduling meetings at major conferences and rotating locations, the NWG ensured that the growing network community could coordinate on protocol decisions and share implementation experiences. This pattern of scheduled, multi-day meetings became the foundation for how standards bodies like the IETF would later operate.
sections.plainLanguage: Having regular meetings at different places helped everyone stay on the same page about how the network should work.
